key_insight: Simple local quantum processes can look highly scrambled in moments (as unitary designs) yet still be efficiently distinguishable from truly random unitaries, so design-like behavior does not imply pseudorandomness.
engineering_relevance: For quantum circuit design, verification, and black-hole-inspired simulation, this means moment-matching metrics alone are insufficient to certify randomness or information scrambling.
method: Construct efficiently samplable distributions over 1- and 2-qubit gates.
Analyze the resulting n-qubit ensemble after O_t(n^2 log^2 n) independent steps.
Compare unitary-design properties against distinguishability by an efficient quantum query algorithm.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximate unitary t-designs with negligible error exp(-Ω(log^2 n)) but still an efficient distinguisher using only O_t(log^2 n) queries.
watch_item: The strongest separation beyond local walks uses highly structured ensembles, so the counterexample may not directly generalize to natural random-circuit implementations.
paper_title: On the pseudorandomness of simple quantum processes
